fact: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.
source_span: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound . The family of bounded evidence accumulation models ... depicts the decision process as a race between competing accumulators ... The decision terminates when the accumulated evidence for one alternative ... reaches a threshold or bound , thereby determining both the choice and the decision time . Confidence in the decision derives from a mapping between the DV and the probability that a decision based on this DV will be correct . In the model, choice, RT and confidence result from the accumulation of noisy momentary evidence as a function of time, until the integral of the evidence (the decision variable, DV) reaches one of two bounds, or for the PDW and confidence tasks, until the stimulus is curtailed.
abstract_sentence: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.

fact: In perception, the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength, characterized by signal-to-noise ratio, on decision speed, accuracy and confidence.
source_span: In perception , the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength , characterized by signal-to-noise ratio , on decision speed , accuracy and confidence . The noisiness of the momentary evidence causes the DV to wander from its starting point ... Noise is the main determinant of both RT and confidence when signal-to-noise is low , that is when choices are more stochastic ( less accurate ) . The overall quality of the fits—across all tasks and both species—indicates that the influence of motion strength and volatility on choice, reaction time and confidence can be explained by a common mechanism of bounded evidence accumulation.
abstract_sentence: In perception, the accumulation of noisy evidence explains how stimulus strength affects decision speed, accuracy, and confidence.

fact: An increase in noise leads to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically higher confidence according to bounded evidence accumulation models.
source_span: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence . Specifically , were it possible to leave unchanged the expectation of each sample of momentary evidence while boosting the noise associated with it , then the bounded accumulation of the noisier samples should lead to ( i ) lower accuracy when the expectation of the momentary evidence is strong , ( ii ) faster reaction times when the momentary evidence is weak , and ( iii ) increased confidence when the momentary evidence is weak . The important point is that by increasing noise , the volatility manipulation accelerates the dispersion of the decision variable away from its expected value and nearer the termination bounds , hence faster RT. Increased volatility should affect confidence because it mimics an increase in the diffusion rate . At low coherences in particular , its main effect on the DV is to accelerate its exodus away from neutral ( probability correct = 0 . 5 ) to more extreme values . Therefore , we predicted that volatility would increase confidence at low coherences , for the same reason that it speeds the RT.
abstract_sentence: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically, higher confidence.

fact: A novel sensory manipulation mimics adding unbiased noise to motion-selective visual cortex, verified by macaque MT/MST neuronal recordings.
source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . We therefore sought a method to manipulate the variance associated with the neural representation of momentary evidence without affecting its mean. We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion (RDM) display, by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence. We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex. Neurons in these areas are known to represent the momentary evidence in tasks identical to those in our study.
abstract_sentence: The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that mimics adding unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, verified by neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.

fact: Increasing noise caused faster decisions and higher confidence in humans and monkeys, while accuracy was minimally affected.

As shown in Figure 4B (lower panel), the proportion of trials the monkey decided to waive the sure-bet option (deciding instead for a riskier direction choice) was greater on the high volatility trials (Equation 19, p<10–6, likelihood-ratio test). Thus, high volatility increased the monkey’s confidence, and did so despite a negligible effect on accuracy.
abstract_sentence: Increasing noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence in both humans and monkeys over a range of stimuli with minimal impairment to accuracy.

fact: Observed thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable computational models of LR neurons to compute the speed of head rotation, despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.

fact: Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism, making quality control mechanisms that dispose of damaged mitochondrial proteins vital for cellular function.
source_span: Proper protein folding is essential for organelle and cell homeostasis . Proteins may fail to achieve or retain their functional conformations due to genetic or environmental insults and cells have evolved elaborate protein quality control ( QC ) mechanisms to combat misfolding . QC systems recognize and refold misfolded proteins and , when not possible , sequester or degrade them to prevent their often deleterious accumulation ( Kevei et al . , 2017 ) . Mitochondrial proteins are subject to ongoing oxidative insults that can result in damage , misfolding , and dysfunction . Mitochondria require mechanisms to eliminate these proteins to maintain organellar integrity and essential functions ( Voos et al . , 2016 ) . Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism . It is therefore vital that QC mechanisms dispose of damaged proteins that can compromise function .
abstract_sentence: Maintaining mitochondrial function requires mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins.

source_span: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase ( E3 ) Ubr1 , while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1 . san1Δ impaired turnover of sam35-2HAts ... ubr1Δ impaired turnover of sen2-1HAts These results establish that San1 and Ubr1 can function as components of the MAD machinery for proteasome-mediated degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts , respectively . Instead , San1 and Ubr1 , which have broad roles as quality control E3s for misfolded cytosolic and nuclear proteins ... , are required to degrade mitochondrial ts- substrates .
abstract_sentence: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase Ubr1, while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1.

fact: Mitochondria-associated degradation ( MAD ) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 , providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD .
source_span: Mitochondria-associated degradation ( MAD ) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 , providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD . Interestingly , both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were strongly stabilized in a conditional yeast strain where three SSA family members are deleted and the fourth ( SSA1 ) is ts- ( ssa1-45ts; ssa1-45ts ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ ) relative to the control strain ( SSA1; SSA1 ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ; Figure 4A ) . Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein using Sis1 DAmP cells slowed the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts , while loss of Ydj1 or its ortholog , Hlj1 , did not . These results establish that the degradation of the mitochondrial QC substrates is dependent on both Hsp70 and Hsp40 chaperones , but independent of nuclear import .
abstract_sentence: Mitochondria-associated degradation of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones and the Hsp40 Sis1, providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in mitochondria-associated degradation.

fact: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1 and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor, Ubx2, are implicated in their degradation.
source_span: In addition to a role for the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex , Doa1 and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor , Ubx2 , are implicated in their degradation . All together, these results indicate that ubiquitinated mitochondrial QC substrates require the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex for efficient proteasomal degradation. In many cases , the involvement of the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex represents another point of convergence ... We found Msp1 to be dispensable for the degradation of mitochondrial ts- substrates . Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were stabilized in conditional Cdc48 , Npl4 , and Ufd1 strains .
abstract_sentence: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1, and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor Ubx2 are implicated in the degradation of misfolded mitochondrial outer membrane proteins.

fact: This study reveals a unique QC pathway comprised of a combination of cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that distinguish it from other cellular QC pathways.
source_span: This study reveals a unique QC pathway comprised of a combination of cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that distinguish it from other cellular QC pathways . These new mitochondrial model substrates have revealed a tightly-coupled degradation pathway at the MOM that requires both cytosolic and mitochondrial machinery . This MAD QC pathway ... is also not identical to any other cellular QC pathway , although there are points of intersection . Our results reveal a requirement for factors not previously implicated in the degradation of native MAD substrates and the combination of components identified defines a distinct QC pathway . The MAD QC pathway characterized here is distinct from this pathway: ts- substrates remain mitochondrial and are degraded independently of ERAD E2s or E3s .
abstract_sentence: This study reveals a unique quality control pathway for misfolded mitochondrial outer membrane proteins that involves both cytosolic and mitochondrial factors and is distinct from other cellular quality control pathways.

fact: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are conserved noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally; miR-9 is one of the most abundant microRNAs in the developing and adult brain.
source_span: MicroRNAs ( miRNAs ) are conserved noncoding RNAs that function as posttranscriptional regulators of gene expression . Importantly , miR-9 is one of the most abundant miRNAs in the developing and adult brain ( Lagos-Quintana et al . , 2002; Krichevsky et al . , 2003 ) .
abstract_sentence: MicroRNAs are conserved noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally, and miR-9 is one of the most abundant microRNAs in the brain.

fact: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development in differentiated neurons was largely unknown before this study.
source_span: Although the function of miR-9 has been well characterized in neural progenitors , its role in dendritic and synaptic development remains largely unknown .
abstract_sentence: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development in differentiated neurons was largely unknown before this study.

fact: The study developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line that allows conditional and spatio-temporal inactivation of the miR-9 family in vivo.
source_span: In order to target miR-9 in vivo , we developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line allowing conditional inactivation of the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner . Here , we describe for the first time a conditional transgenic sponge mouse model . In summary , we describe the first transgenic sponge mouse line that allows for conditional inactivation of an miRNA family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner . This newly generated mouse line conditionally expresses the GFP-FC-miR-9-sponge in the CNS.
abstract_sentence: A transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line was developed to conditionally inactivate the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner in vivo.

fact: Using the miR-9 sponge mouse, the study found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.
source_span: Using this novel approach , we found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo . Using the latter , we revealed a novel developmental role of miR-9 in the postmitotic differentiation of neurons , as a key regulator of dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo . Pyramidal CA1 neurons from miR-9-SpNestin-Cre mice exhibited a reduction in total dendritic length and arborization complexity compared to control littermates (miR-9-Spfl-Stop). miR-9 sponge-transfected neurons show a reduced total dendritic length and reduced dendritic complexity.
abstract_sentence: Using the miR-9 sponge mouse, miR-9 was found to control dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.

fact: miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth.
source_span: Furthermore , we demonstrate that miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth . We found that 13 out of 26 miR-9 predicted targets were upregulated in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons. Interestingly, one of the upregulated mRNAs encodes the global transcriptional repressor element 1 (RE-1) silencing transcription factor (REST/NRSF). Moreover, miR-9 sponges reversed the miR-9-induced downregulation of REST in HEK-293 cells further demonstrating the regulatory effect of miR-9 on REST levels. We observed that shREST transfection strongly rescued the dendritic growth defects in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons, indicating that increased REST level is indeed the major mediator of miR-9 effects on dendritic growth.
abstract_sentence: miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth.

fact: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.
source_span: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures .
abstract_sentence: Vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.

fact: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.
source_span: However , thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens .
abstract_sentence: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.

fact: Ross River virus is an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia, the Pacific Islands, and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide.
source_span: We built a mechanistic model for the thermal response of Ross River virus , an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia , Pacific Islands , and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide .
abstract_sentence: A mechanistic model was built for the thermal response of Ross River virus, an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia and nearby regions.

fact: Transmission of Ross River virus peaks at moderate temperatures (26.4°C) and declines to zero at thermal limits of 17.0°C and 31.5°C.
source_span: Transmission peaks at moderate temperatures ( 26 . 4°C ) and declines to zero at thermal limits ( 17 . 0 and 31 . 5°C ) . Transmission potential ( relative R0 from the full R0 model ) peaked at 26 . 4°C , and was positive from 17 . 0–31 . 5°C ( Figure 3 ) . The optimal temperature for transmission is moderate ( 26–27°C; Figure 3 ) , and largely determined by the thermal response of adult mosquito lifespan ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2 ) .
abstract_sentence: Ross River virus transmission peaks at moderate temperatures around 26.4°C and declines to zero below 17.0°C and above 31.5°C.

fact: The mechanistic model accurately predicts that Ross River virus transmission is year-round endemic in tropical regions but seasonal in temperate areas.
source_span: The model accurately predicts that transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas , resulting in the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases . Temperature suitability for RRV transmission varies seasonally across Australia ... In subtropical and temperate locations ... low temperatures force R0 to zero for part of the year ... By contrast , in tropical , northern Australia ... the temperature remains suitable throughout the year ... As predicted by the model ( Figures 5 and 6 ) , RRV is endemic in tropical Australia , with little seasonal variation in transmission potential due to temperature , and seasonally epidemic in subtropical and temperate Australia ( Weinstein , 1997 ) .
abstract_sentence: The model accurately predicts that Ross River virus transmission is year-round endemic in tropical regions but seasonal in temperate areas.

fact: Climate warming will likely increase Ross River virus transmission in temperate areas where most Australians live but decrease transmission in tropical areas where temperatures are near the thermal optimum.
source_span: Climate warming will likely increase transmission in temperate areas ( where most Australians live ) but decrease transmission in tropical areas where mean temperatures are already near the thermal optimum . Climate warming will likely increase the geographic and seasonal range of transmission potential in temperate , southern Australia where most Australians live . However , climate change will likely decrease transmission potential in tropical areas like Darwin , where moderate warming ( ~3°C ) would push temperatures above the upper thermal limit for transmission for most of the year ( Figure 5 ) .
abstract_sentence: Climate warming will likely increase Ross River virus transmission in temperate areas where most Australians live but decrease transmission in tropical areas where temperatures are near the thermal optimum.

fact: Nonlinear mechanistic models are critical for estimating temperature impacts on Ross River virus transmission because temperature increases can have positive, negligible, or negative effects depending on the thermal response curve position.
source_span: A nonlinear mechanistic model is critical for estimating temperature impacts on transmission because the effect of increasing temperature by a few degrees can have a positive , negligible , or negative impact on R0 along different parts of the thermal response curve . Nonlinear thermal responses are particularly important for predicting how transmission will change under future climate regimes .
abstract_sentence: Nonlinear mechanistic models are critical for estimating temperature impacts on Ross River virus transmission because temperature increases can have positive, negligible, or negative effects depending on the thermal response curve position.

fact: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been observed for decades, but their specific behavioral correlates remain unclear.
source_span: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades , yet their behavioral correlates remain unresolved .
abstract_sentence: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been observed for decades, but their specific behavioral correlates remain unclear.

fact: Three macaque monkeys were trained to volitionally modulate their motor cortical beta oscillations using a neurofeedback task before reaching.
source_span: To investigate how changes in population neural activity , beta oscillations , and behavior are linked , we recorded multi-scale neural activity from motor cortex while three macaques performed a novel neurofeedback task . Subjects volitionally brought their beta oscillatory power to an instructed state and subsequently executed an arm reach . To explore how beta oscillations reflect changes in spiking activity and movement parameters , we trained three macaque monkeys to perform a typical center-out arm-reaching task ( CO task , Figure 1a ) , and a novel sequential beta neurofeedback arm-reaching task ( NR task , Figure 1b ) . Three male rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) were chronically implanted with arrays of 128 Teflon-coated tungsten microwire electrodes... in the left upper arm area of primary motor cortex (M1) and posterior dorsal premotor cortex (PMd).
abstract_sentence: The study used a novel neurofeedback task in which three macaque monkeys volitionally modulated their motor cortical beta oscillatory power before performing an arm reach.

fact: Monkeys modulated their motor cortical beta power to specific target levels using neurofeedback before performing reaching movements.
source_span: Subjects modulated endogenous motor cortical local field potential signals to move the vertical position of the beta cursor . Specifically , the cursor was controlled by a spectral estimate of beta band power normalized by a spectral estimate of broadband ( 1–100 Hz ) power ... When the beta cursor fell in the beta target , subjects were required to hold within the beta target for 450 ms . After successful completion , both the beta cursor and beta target disappeared , cueing that the reaching epoch had begun ... Subjects then executed a right-arm reach from the central target to a peripheral target to receive a liquid reward . The neurofeedback epoch accomplished the goal of bringing beta power to different levels shown by plotting mean normalized beta power for the last 1 s of the neurofeedback epoch ... At the time of the go cue there is a significant group difference in normalized beta power for the four different neurofeedback target conditions Mean traces show that high and low beta targets were achieved by increasing and decreasing beta power , respectively .
abstract_sentence: Subjects volitionally brought their beta oscillatory power to an instructed state and subsequently executed an arm reach.

fact: Lower beta power before reaching is associated with faster movement onset; higher beta power delays movement start.
source_span: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power . In all three animals, trials with high beta power targets had subsequent reaches with slower movement onset times (Figure 3a–c, two-tailed Cuzick’s test, Monkey S: z = 5.763, p=8.267e-09, n = 1183, Monkey C: z = 11.987, p<5e-20, n = 2168, Monkey G: z = 5.856, p=4.729e-09, n = 1028). Despite the different approaches that were taken to increase and decrease beta power across animals there is still a consistent effect of high versus low beta power on movement onset times , increasing confidence that the oscillation is a reliable marker of the observed behavior .
abstract_sentence: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power.

fact: Neural population activity patterns are further from movement initiation during beta oscillations, whether induced by neurofeedback or naturally occurring.
source_span: Further , population neural activity was found to shift farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks . In Figure 7b , traces are aligned to the go cue , showing that during the neurofeedback epoch prior to the go cue , the high beta target ( red ) maintains a much greater distance from the MO threshold than the low and mid-low beta targets ( green and blue ) . At the time of the go cue the high beta target is further from the MO threshold than the lower beta targets , suggesting that subjects must traverse a greater neural distance to arrive at the MO threshold , which may take longer resulting in a longer MOT . Here , we report both changes in motor behavior following performance of neurofeedback during a sequential neurofeedback-reaching task , and a neural population shift that mirrors the observed change in motor behavior . Notably , this shift in neural population was also seen in naturally occurring beta oscillations during reaching tasks , suggesting that beta oscillations reflect a common signature of spiking patterns even in different task contexts . When populations of neurons generate beta oscillations , their patterns are further from movement onset threshold than when they do not generate oscillations . In both the CO and NR tasks , on-beta PreMO bins exhibit further distances from the MO threshold than off-beta PreMO bins ... We propose that neural populations must stop generating beta oscillations before they can initiate specific preparatory and movement generating patterns ... Thus , the generation of beta oscillations favors a low-risk state in which neural populations will not accidentally create patterns that cause movement , and in exchange compromise their readiness for upcoming movements .
abstract_sentence: Population neural activity was found to shift farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks.

fact: The study demonstrates that beta oscillations correspond to neural states that slow the start of movement.
source_span: This finding establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity . Our result that volitionally increasing and decreasing motor cortical beta power with neurofeedback precedes slower and faster movement onset times supports the hypothesis that beta oscillations are linked to neural patterns that slow onset of new movements ( Gilbertson et al . , 2005 ). The results from this study show that beta band frequencies are a marker of slowed movement onset.
abstract_sentence: This finding establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity.

fact: Unlike Marburg, Dengue, and KSHV viruses that benefit from Nrf2 activation, HIV infection is blocked through Nrf2 activation.
source_span: Marburg virus , the Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus ( KSHV ) and Dengue virus all activate , and benefit from , expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) . Together this work shows that , in contrast to Marburg , Dengue and KSHV , HIV is blocked through Nrf2 and sets the stage for discovering the mechanism underlying this restriction . Finally , the discovery that Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages stands in contrast with recent work showing that Marburg and Dengue virus as well as KSHV initiate and benefit from increased Nrf2 expression [30 , 32 , 34 , 41] .
abstract_sentence: Some viruses activate and benefit from Nrf2, but HIV is blocked by Nrf2 activation.

fact: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection had not been tested prior to this study.
source_span: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus ( HIV ) infection has not been tested .
abstract_sentence: The impact of Nrf2 activation on HIV infection had not been tested before this study.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN), a compound produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage, mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression.
source_span: Sulforaphane ( SFN ) , produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage , mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression . SFN is a powerful mobilizer of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) [22–24] . Nrf2 , a master regulator of the antioxidant response [25 , 26] , ... SFN acts through Nrf2 to execute the majority of its known functions [44–46] . As expected , SFN significantly increased levels of Nrf2 as well as of the Nrf2-regulated genes NQO1 and GCLM ( Fig 8 ) .
abstract_sentence: Sulforaphane (SFN) from cruciferous vegetables activates Nrf2 to strongly change gene expression.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.
source_span: Here we show for the first time that SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells . Thus, SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells. SFN does not block infection in all cell-types and ... the dependence in macrophages solely on Nrf2 also indicates that SFN is neither inhibiting HIV directly by modifying a viral component nor is it modifying and thereby inhibiting a cellular component that the virus needs for successful infection . Further investigation will be required to determine why SFN fails to block infection in T cells , whether the same pathway could be exploited there as well or whether the restriction can be activated directly by other means .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.

fact: siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment.
source_span: Similarly SFN blocks infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines , but not in other cell lines tested . siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment . In the absence of SFN , depletion of Nrf2 caused a significant increase in luciferase activity indicating that Nrf2 is detrimental to HIV infection in macrophages and that the basal level of Nrf2 that is present in macrophages is sufficient for establishing some anti-viral activity ( Fig 6D ) . Specifically , boosting Nrf2 counters infection while Nrf2 depletion supports infection .
abstract_sentence: Depleting Nrf2 increases HIV infection in macrophages and reduces SFN’s antiviral effect, showing the antiviral activity depends on Nrf2.

fact: Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment .
source_span: Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment . Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment . SFN blocks single-round HIV-1 and HIV-2 infections ( Fig 4 ) . DMF and MMF , like SFN , increase levels of Nrf2 [55] , suggesting that these compounds also block HIV in macrophages through Nrf2 .
abstract_sentence: SFN enhances an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in macrophages.

fact: SFN treatment blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before the formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.
source_span: We further found that , like the type I interferon-induced cellular anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 , SFN treatment blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles . This limits the Nrf2-mediated block to steps that extend from attachment of the virus to the cell through transcription from the provirus . ... The vehicle- and SFN-treated samples showed similar levels of late reverse transcription product , indicating that SFN , unlike AZT , did not hinder replication steps from viral entry through reverse transcription ( Fig 7A ) . When we tested for 2-LTR circles ... we found that these were clearly decreased in the AZT and SFN samples relative to the vehicle controls ( Fig 7B ) . Alu-PCR , testing for integrated proviral sequences , also showed that these were similarly decreased in AZT- and SFN-treated cultures to levels that were significantly lower than in the vehicle-treated controls ( Fig 7C ) . We found that SFN counters infection whether viral entry is mediated through HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins ( Figs 1B versus 5E ) . This suggests a post-entry block as these glycoproteins engage different entry mechanisms .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before 2-LTR circle formation, similar to antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.

fact: SFN does not upregulate the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during its inhibition of HIV infection.
source_span: Interestingly however , neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated . SFN did not significantly change levels of either SAMHD1 or MX2 . Conversely , IFNα treatment increased levels of MX2 as expected . We immunoblotted lysates of mock- and SFN-treated U937 cells for SAMHD1 and found that while SAMHD1 was readily detected in THP1 lysates, it remained undetectable in U937 lysates under the conditions tested. This indicates that SFN does not block HIV by increasing SAMHD1 levels.
abstract_sentence: SFN does not increase levels of antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during HIV inhibition.

fact: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, revealing a novel way to trigger antiviral inhibition.
source_span: This shows for the first time that Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition . We thus have discovered in SFN , a new way to activate an anti-viral state that HIV may not have previously encountered . It is therefore unlikely that the virus has developed an effective countermeasure .
abstract_sentence: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, revealing a novel antiviral mechanism.

fact: Aedes-borne arboviruses such as dengue and Zika continue to cause epidemics worldwide.
source_span: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to precipitate epidemics worldwide .
abstract_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to cause epidemics worldwide.

fact: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.
source_span: In Dominican Republic , the appearance of Zika virus cases that closely followed a large dengue epidemic provided an opportunity to study the different transmission drivers behind these two flaviviruses . The Dominican Republic was similarly affected . As this outbreak abated , the first cases of Zika were detected . Then by week 52 of 2016 , 5 , 235 Zika patients ( 5 . 5 per 10 , 000 population ) , 22 cases of infant microcephaly and 600 cases of Guillain-Barre syndrome ( GBS ) had been reported .
abstract_sentence: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.

fact: Retrospective surveillance data from the Dominican Republic were used to analyze national outbreaks of dengue, Zika, and associated Guillain-Barre syndrome cases.
source_span: Retrospective datasets were used to collect information on the populations at risk and descriptive statistics were used to describe the outbreaks on a national scale .
abstract_sentence: Retrospective surveillance data from the Dominican Republic were used to analyze national outbreaks of dengue, Zika, and associated Guillain-Barre syndrome cases.

fact: Dengue cases were predominantly reported in individuals under 20 years old, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.
source_span: Expectedly , box plots showed that 75% of dengue was reported in those aged <20 years while Zika infections were more widely dispersed among the population . Boxplots established the distribution of cases among the population ... and revealed that 75% of all dengue cases occurred before the age of 20 compared with ~42 for Zika.
abstract_sentence: Dengue cases were predominantly reported in individuals under 20 years old, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.

fact: Dengue attack rates were slightly higher in males compared to females in the Dominican Republic.
source_span: Dengue attack rates were marginally higher among males at 25 . 9 per 10 , 000 population vs . 21 . 5 per 10 , 000 population for females . Age-adjusted attack rates of dengue in males was 25.9 per 10,000 population vs. 21.5 per 10,000 population in females. As a percentage, dengue infections were higher among men than women: 54.5% ... vs. 45.5% ... respectively.
abstract_sentence: Dengue attack rates were slightly higher in males compared to females in the Dominican Republic.

fact: Zika infections were significantly more common among females, with females accounting for 73.8% of cases and higher age-adjusted attack rates than males.
source_span: Zika infections appeared to be highly clustered among females ( 73 . 8% ( 95% CI 72 . 6% , 75 . 0%; p<0 . 05 ) ) ; age-adjusted Zika attack rates among females were 7 . 64 per 10 , 000 population compared with 2 . 72 per 10 , 000 population among males . By comparison, Zika infection was markedly lower among men than women: 26.2% ... vs. 73.8% ... respectively.
abstract_sentence: Zika infections were significantly more common among females, with females accounting for 73.8% of cases and higher age-adjusted attack rates than males.

fact: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than males, indicating greater transmission potential among females.
source_span: R0 calculations stratified by sex also showed a significantly higher metric among females: 1 . 84 ( 1 . 82 , 1 . 87; p<0 . 05 ) when compared to males at 1 . 72 ( 1 . 69 , 1 . 75; p<0 . 05 ) . National R0 Zika calculations gave a national basic reproduction number of 1.80 ... Stratifying by sex, the national R0 for males was 1.72 ... and 1.84 ... for females.
abstract_sentence: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than males, indicating greater transmission potential among females.

fact: Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.
source_span: However , GBS attack rates stratified by sex revealed slightly higher risk in males vs . females , at 0 . 62 and 0 . 57 per 10 , 000 population respectively .
abstract_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.

fact: Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.
source_span: Evidence suggests little impact of existing dengue immunity on reported attack rates of Zika at the population level .
abstract_sentence: Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.

fact: Community awareness campaigns likely increased health-seeking behavior and reporting among women of reproductive age during the Zika outbreak, though biological susceptibility cannot be ruled out.
source_span: The findings indicate that community awareness campaigns , through influencing short-term health seeking behaviour , remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women of reproductive age , although biological susceptibility cannot yet be ruled out . Evidence also suggests a greater burden of Zika among women, however this is most likely due to increased health-seeking behaviour rather than biological mechanisms. If correct, targeted advocacy campaigns are effective at changing short-term behaviour and are recommended during Zika epidemics.
abstract_sentence: Community awareness campaigns likely increased health-seeking behavior and reporting among women of reproductive age during the Zika outbreak, though biological susceptibility cannot be ruled out.

fact: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks to improve detection and response.
source_span: Media campaigns and screening are therefore recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks .
abstract_sentence: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks to improve detection and response.

fact: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.
source_span: Under nitrogen deprivation , filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena undergo a process of development , resulting in a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen deprivation, Anabaena filaments develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.

fact: The transcription factor HetR is essential for heterocyst differentiation in Anabaena and was studied using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion to accurately measure gene expression fluctuations.
source_span: We studied the statistics of fluctuations of gene expression of HetR , a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation , both under steady-state growth in nitrogen-rich conditions and at different times following nitrogen deprivation , using a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion . Our study was conducted using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion , thereby avoiding any contribution to fluctuations stemming from cell-cell variability in plasmid copy number , which would preclude accurate evaluation of both noise and cell-cell correlations in expression . As a reporter , a fusion to a fragment of the N-terminal part of the protein was constructed rather than a traditional transcriptional fusion because with the N-terminal translational fusion , expression of the gene with all its transcription and translation start signals is tested .
abstract_sentence: HetR is a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation, studied using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion to measure expression fluctuations under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions.

fact: Gene expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells along Anabaena filaments are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells.
source_span: Statistical analysis of fluorescence at the individual cell level in wild-type and mutant filaments demonstrates that expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled , with a characteristic spatial range of circa two to three cells , setting the scale for cellular interactions along a filament . These correlations extend to two to three cells , setting the scale for cellular interactions along a filament . The spatial autocorrelation function of hetR-gfp expression along filaments shows that correlations between neighboring cells die out after two to three cells , a range of correlations that is shorter than the characteristic scale of developmental patterns . Irrespective of the strain , the behavior illustrated in Fig . 3B and 3C indicates that gene expression between cells under nitrogen-rich conditions is correlated up to distances of two to three cells .
abstract_sentence: Expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells along Anabaena filaments are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells, defining the scale of cellular interactions.

fact: Intercellular molecular transfer contributes more to correlations in hetR expression between cells than cell division.
source_span: Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division . We stress that the dominant part of the observed correlations must derive from intercellular molecular transfer: had the measured correlations been due exclusively to cell division , there would be no difference between the autocorrelation functions pertaining to the different mutant strains .
abstract_sentence: Correlations in hetR expression between cells mainly arise from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.

fact: Primordial fluctuations in hetR-gfp expression under nitrogen-rich conditions are statistically similar to those at early times after nitrogen deprivation, suggesting continuity in gene expression fluctuations during developmental triggering.
source_span: Our measurements of the statistical properties of fluctuations in gene expression of hetR-gfp well after the developmental network has sensed nitrogen step-down , but possibly before a final commitment has been established show that the primordial fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions and those at early times after nitrogen step-down , e . g . 3 hours , are statistically similar . This suggests that there is continuity between the two , and fluctuations found once the developmental network has been triggered , build up from those Our results show that fluctuations can build up from an underlying pattern of expression under nitrogen-replete conditions in which important regulators are already expressed, and evolve to intermediate states in which fluctuations are positively correlated in clusters of cells. These latter resolve after commitment into single heterocysts using lateral inhibition, supporting a two-stage model of development.
abstract_sentence: Fluctuations in hetR expression under nitrogen-rich conditions are statistically similar to those shortly after nitrogen deprivation, suggesting that developmental fluctuations build on pre-existing patterns.

fact: Basal expression of PatS, cell-cell communication influenced by SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression and its distribution along filaments under nitrogen-rich conditions.
source_span: We found that under nitrogen-rich conditions , basal , steady-state expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS , cell-cell communication influenced by the septal protein SepJ and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression and its distribution along filaments . Together , these facts highlight again the fundamental role that the PatS inhibitor plays in determining the fluctuations along a filament . Together , these findings suggest that positive auto-regulation is essential to build up the large levels of HetR needed for progression of differentiation in some cells and not in others , consistent with the lack of heterocyst formation in this mutant [22 , 49] . The genetic cascade leading to heterocyst formation in cyanobacterial filaments is initiated by the NtcA transcription factor , which senses the low intracellular nitrogen concentration through the levels of 2-oxoglutarate . The master regulator of differentiation HetR , which positively auto-regulates its own expression , is also induced early after nitrogen step-down in an NtcA-dependent way .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen-rich conditions, basal expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS, cell-cell communication via the septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of hetR expression fluctuations and distribution along filaments.

fact: PatS and HetN act as early and late inhibitors of heterocyst differentiation respectively, and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in their specificity affecting hetR expression patterns.
source_span: A comparison between the expression of hetR-gfp under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions highlights the differences between the two HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN , as well as the differences in specificity between the septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD . In contrast to those positive factors , an inhibitor of heterocyst differentiation at early times , PatS , and another inhibitor that is produced at later times , HetN , suppress the differentiation of vegetative cells into nitrogen-fixing heterocysts . Both inhibitors share the amino acid motif ERGSGR in their sequence , which may act by inhibiting HetR . The hetR-gfp fusion was transferred to wild-type Anabaena ( WT ) and mutant strains with deletions in the patS regulatory gene [33] , in the hetN regulatory gene [27] , in the sepJ gene encoding septal protein SepJ [19] , and in the fraC and fraD genes encoding septal proteins FraC and FraD [20] ...
abstract_sentence: The HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN differ in their roles and timing during heterocyst pattern formation, and septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in specificity.

fact: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochastic gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena filaments.
source_span: Our results show that proteins involved in these basic ingredients combine together in the presence of inevitable stochasticity in gene expression , to control the coupled fluctuations of gene expression that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in this organism . Unlike unicellular organisms , multicellular organisms can use cell-cell communication in order to control noise in gene expression . Evidence of such communication has been provided in the case of the Drosophila embryo ... Intercellular communication is likely an important factor for determining heterocyst pattern formation . Variations in gene expression between cells play a key role in determining cellular decisions during developmental processes [14 , 43] .
abstract_sentence: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochastic gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that generate the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena filaments.

fact: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback for each mapping is provided alternately.
source_span: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings ( dual-adaptation ) when feedback for each is provided alternately .
abstract_sentence: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback for each is provided alternately.

fact: Learned context cues associated with each visuomotor mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings.
source_span: Moreover , learned context cues associated with each mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings . This type of associative learning is quite general and even extents to contextual cues that are not necessarily directly task relevant . For instance , the colour of a target for a pointing task normally is irrelevant for how we perform the pointing movement . However , we can learn that we have to point a certain extent to the right for blue targets and to the left for red ones in order to “hit” them [9] .
abstract_sentence: Learned context cues associated with each visuomotor mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings.

fact: Little is known about the associative learning between cue and required visuomotor mapping, and how learning generalises to novel but similar conditions.
source_span: However , little is known about the associative learning between cue and required visuomotor mapping , and how learning generalises to novel but similar conditions . It is important to note , however , that in most of these studies the role of the learned associations was investigated for only two discrete association-stimulus/visuomotor-mapping pairings . That is , in many of these studies , the context cue could often only have one of two discrete states: the presence or absence of the cue . In this case , testing conditions cannot go beyond the specifically trained pairings to see how the trained pairings generalise to novel conditions ( a cue cannot be half present ) . However , many cues , like the location of targets when learning the distortions for a single pair of glasses , can vary in a continuous manner . The question arises how learning for a discrete number of trained pairings affects the learning rate and generalises to novel conditions on the same continuous cue scale . We investigated the learning of the association between previously irrelevant target shape cues and behaviourally relevant visuomotor mappings.
abstract_sentence: Little is known about how associative learning between cues and required visuomotor mappings generalises to novel but similar conditions.

fact: Participants performed a rapid target-pointing task while visual feedback was manipulated with horizontal offsets dependent on target shape.
source_span: To investigate these questions , participants performed a rapid target-pointing task while we manipulated the offset between visual feedback and movement end-points . The visual feedback was presented with horizontal offsets of different amounts , dependent on the targets shape . By manipulating the location of this feedback relative to the pointing position on the tablet we can simulate different visuomotor mappings . That is , different motor responses are required to bring the feedback on the target location .
abstract_sentence: Participants performed a rapid target-pointing task with visual feedback offsets dependent on target shape to study visuomotor mapping learning.

fact: Participants needed to use different visuomotor mappings between target location and required motor response depending on the target shape in order to “hit” it.
source_span: Participants thus needed to use different visuomotor mappings between target location and required motor response depending on the target shape in order to “hit” it . Participants performed a target-pointing task in which we manipulated the spatial mapping of the visual feedback that participants received upon completion of their pointing movements. Since we were interested in the transfer of learning we wanted to increase the chance for learning. Therefore, in Experiment 2 we informed participants about the fact that different shapes would need different pointing behaviours. However, the participants were not informed about the particular contingencies between the shape and mapping which they had to deduce themselves. In Experiment 2 and 3 participants were informed about the fact that different shapes would need different pointing behaviours. However, participants were not informed about the particular shape-mapping contingencies, which they had to deduce themselves.
abstract_sentence: Participants needed to use different visuomotor mappings depending on the target shape to successfully hit the target.

fact: The target shapes were taken from a continuous set of shapes, morphed between spiky and circular shapes.
source_span: The target shapes were taken from a continuous set of shapes , morphed between spiky and circular shapes . In the present study we circumvented these problems by investigating how learning and generalisation occurs for associations with a task-irrelevant property of the target in a rapid pointing task . Here , we chose target shape as the contextual cue that ranged from circular to spiky on a continuous scale ( see Fig . 1 , cf 3 ) .
abstract_sentence: Target shapes were morphed continuously between spiky and circular shapes to create a continuous cue dimension.

fact: After training we tested participants performance, without feedback, on different target shapes that had not been learned previously.
source_span: After training we tested participants performance , without feedback , on different target shapes that had not been learned previously . In the first experiment, participants were trained on two specific target shape/mapping contingencies... Afterwards, using catch trials... we tested participants’ pointing performance to target shapes that had not been used explicitly during training. The other 60 trials were catch trials in which we tested the transfer of training to other target shapes. On catch trials participants did not receive any visual feedback indicating the pointing end-point ...
abstract_sentence: After training, participants were tested without feedback on novel target shapes that had not been learned previously.

fact: We compared two hypotheses: explicit linear generalisation and an implicit Bayesian model predicting categorisation-like generalisation.
source_span: We compared two hypotheses . First , we hypothesised that participants could ( explicitly ) extract the linear relationship between target shape and visuomotor mapping and generalise accordingly . Second , using previous findings of visuomotor learning , we developed a ( implicit ) Bayesian learning model that predicts generalisation that is more consistent with categorisation ( i . e . use one mapping or the other ) .
abstract_sentence: The study compared an explicit linear generalisation hypothesis with an implicit Bayesian learning model predicting categorisation-like generalisation.

fact: Learning the associations requires explicit awareness of the cues’ role; participants apply the mapping corresponding to the trained shape most similar to the current one, consistent with the Bayesian learning model.
source_span: The experimental results show that , although learning the associations requires explicit awareness of the cues’ role , participants apply the mapping corresponding to the trained shape that is most similar to the current one , consistent with the Bayesian learning model . For learning to occur , participants needed to be aware of the role that the shape-cue was playing . At least for Experiment 1 , where participants were not informed about the role of the target shape prior to the experiment , only those participants learned who consciously noticed the role of the shape . Participants who had not noticed the shape-mapping contingency also did not learn to adjust their behaviour differentially corresponding to the target shape. For the participants that learned the shape-mapping contingencies... there is some form of transfer of learning from the trained shape-mapping contingencies to the other shapes along the scale... the results for all participants but one conformed with this linear hypothesis.
abstract_sentence: Learning the associations between cues and visuomotor mappings requires explicit awareness of the cues’ role, and participants generalise by applying the mapping corresponding to the trained shape most similar to the current shape.

fact: The Bayesian learning model predicts that learning should slow down with increased numbers of training pairs, which was confirmed by the present results.
source_span: Furthermore , the Bayesian learning model predicts that learning should slow down with increased numbers of training pairs , which was confirmed by the present results . Furthermore, the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters predicts slower learning rates with an increased number of training pairs as was also observed experimentally. In different experiments we varied the number of training pairs ( target shape/mapping pairings ) to investigate differences due to the amount of information available for extracting the linear rule for generalisation to novel shapes as well as how the number of training pairs affects learning rates . The model therefore predicts a slow down of the overall learning rate with an increased number of shape-mapping pairs to be learned .
abstract_sentence: The Bayesian learning model predicts that learning slows down with increased numbers of training pairs, which was confirmed experimentally.

fact: The Bayesian learning model corresponds well with empirical results and poses a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings.
source_span: In short , we found a good correspondence between the Bayesian learning model and the empirical results indicating that this model poses a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings . Simulations from this model were compared to the empirical results as an alternative hypothesis to the linear generalisation rule .
abstract_sentence: The Bayesian learning model provides a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings.

fact: Resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward control and elimination goals for NTDs.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy... have been targeted for control or elimination, but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2].
abstract_sentence: Many NTD-endemic countries have not been able to launch or scale-up programs because they lack necessary baseline data and face resource constraints.

source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
abstract_sentence: Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated mapping approach could result in significant resource savings.

source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
abstract_sentence: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.

source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained .

source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .

source_span: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .

source_span: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies .

fact: Stem cells have an innate ability to occupy their stem cell niche, which is optimized to house stem cells.
source_span: Stem cells have an innate ability to occupy their stem cell niche , which in turn , is optimized to house stem cells .
abstract_sentence: Stem cells have an innate ability to occupy their stem cell niche, which is optimized to house stem cells.

fact: Organ aging is associated with reduced stem cell occupancy in the niche, but the mechanisms involved are poorly understood.
source_span: Organ aging is associated with reduced stem cell occupancy in the niche , but the mechanisms involved are poorly understood .
abstract_sentence: Organ aging is associated with reduced stem cell occupancy in the niche, but the mechanisms involved are poorly understood.

fact: Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells (GSCs), resulting in their removal from the niche.
source_span: Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells ( GSCs ) , and this results in their removal from the niche . We observed a 20% increase of E(spl)m7-lacZ expression in aged GSCs as compared to their younger counterparts... GSCs in the niche exhibit various levels of enhanced Notch signaling during aging, and higher Notch signaling correlates with earlier GSC loss due to decreased GSC-niche attachment.
abstract_sentence: Notch signaling is increased with age in Drosophila female germline stem cells (GSCs), resulting in their removal from the niche.

fact: GSCs with low levels of Notch signaling exhibit increased adhesiveness to the niche, out-competing neighbors with higher Notch levels through regulation of E-cadherin expression.
source_span: Clonal analysis revealed that GSCs with low levels of Notch signaling exhibit increased adhesiveness to the niche , thereby out-competing their neighbors with higher levels of Notch; adhesiveness is altered through regulation of E-cadherin expression . E-cadherin is a cell-cell adhesion molecule required for GSC-niche adhesion [12]; we found that its expression was significantly increased in mutant GSC-niche junctions... Notch signaling controls GSC competitiveness in an E-cadherin-dependent manner. Overexpression of NNICD in GSCs decreased E-cadherin expression at GSC-niche junctions and accelerated aging-dependent GSC loss.
abstract_sentence: GSCs with low levels of Notch signaling exhibit increased adhesiveness to the niche, out-competing neighbors with higher Notch levels through regulation of E-cadherin expression.

fact: Experimental enhancement of Notch signaling in GSCs accelerates their age-dependent loss from the niche, partially mediated by Sex lethal.
source_span: Experimental enhancement of Notch signaling in GSCs hastens their age-dependent loss from the niche , and such loss is at least partially mediated by Sex lethal . The use of sxlRNAi under the control of a germ cell-specific driver to knock down Sxl expression in GSCs also resulted in a 47% increase of Notch signaling in GSCs... and promoted GSC loss. Our results suggest that the induction of Notch signaling with age in GSCs is at least partly mediated by Sxl.
abstract_sentence: Experimental enhancement of Notch signaling in GSCs accelerates their age-dependent loss from the niche, partially mediated by Sex lethal.

fact: Disruption of Notch signaling in GSCs does not delay GSC loss during aging and does not affect BMP signaling, which promotes GSC self-renewal.
source_span: However , disruption of Notch signaling in GSCs does not delay GSC loss during aging , and nor does it affect BMP signaling , which promotes self-renewal of GSCs . However , the levels of two well-established reporters of BMP signaling [30] , phosphorylated ( p ) Mad ( pMad ) and Dad-lacZ , were unaffected in Notch signaling-defective GSCs , as compared to their neighboring control GSCs . Although inhibition of Notch expression increased E-cadherin expression at the GSC-niche junction, this was not sufficient to suppress age-dependent GSC loss.
abstract_sentence: Disruption of Notch signaling in GSCs does not delay GSC loss during aging and does not affect BMP signaling, which promotes GSC self-renewal.

fact: Notch activation in the niche cells, which maintains niche integrity and mediates GSC retention, is reduced with age.
source_span: Finally , we show that in contrast to GSCs , Notch activation in the niche ( which maintains niche integrity , and thus mediates GSC retention ) is reduced with age , indicating that Notch signaling regulates GSC niche occupancy both intrinsically and extrinsically . We observed that Notch signaling in the niche and GSCs was affected by age in different ways; during aging , Notch signaling was decreased in the niche , but increased in GSCs .
abstract_sentence: Notch activation in the niche cells, which maintains niche integrity and mediates GSC retention, is reduced with age.

fact: Notch signaling regulates GSC-niche adhesion in response to aging, a novel role relevant also to metastatic cancer cells where Notch suppresses cell adhesion.
source_span: Our findings expose a novel role of Notch signaling in controlling GSC-niche adhesion in response to aging , and are also of relevance to metastatic cancer cells , in which Notch signaling suppresses cell adhesion .
abstract_sentence: Notch signaling regulates GSC-niche adhesion in response to aging, a novel role relevant also to metastatic cancer cells where Notch suppresses cell adhesion.

fact: HIV infection cannot currently be cured but can be controlled by combination treatment with multiple anti-retroviral drugs.

fact: Different viral genotypes occur in virtually every individual HIV patient, raising the question of which drug combination to use to achieve effective treatment.
