abstract_sentence: Different viral genotypes occur in virtually every individual HIV patient, raising the question of which drug combination is most effective for treatment.

fact: Computational models using viral genotypic and clinical phenotypic data can predict optimal HIV treatment regimens for individual patients.
source_span: With the availability of viral genotypic data and clinical phenotypic data, it has become possible to create computational models able to predict an optimal treatment regimen for an individual patient.
abstract_sentence: Computational models using viral genotypic and clinical phenotypic data can predict optimal HIV treatment regimens for individual patients.

fact: Current models are based only on sequence data derived from viral genotyping; chemical similarity of drugs is not considered.
source_span: Current models are based only on sequence data derived from viral genotyping; chemical similarity of drugs is not considered.
abstract_sentence: Current HIV resistance prediction models are based only on viral sequence data and do not consider chemical similarity of drugs.

fact: Proteochemometric (PCM) modeling combines chemical and protein target properties in a single bioactivity model to improve drug resistance prediction.
source_span: Hence it is likely that also for established drugs , chemical similarity can improve models by explicitly taking the concept of drug – target interaction into account , which is then combined with mutational information of the drug target itself . This technique is called proteochemometric ( PCM ) modeling .
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric (PCM) modeling combines mutant data and drug chemical data to improve prediction of drug resistance by explicitly considering drug-target interactions.

fact: The dataset included about 300,000 drug-mutant bioactivity data points, covering 4 NNRTI, 8 NRTI, and 9 PI drugs, and tens of thousands of mutants.
source_span: Our dataset was a large scale clinical database of genotypic and phenotypic information (in total ca. 300,000 drug-mutant bioactivity data points, 4 (NNRTI), 8 (NRTI) or 9 (PI) drugs, and 10,700 (NNRTI) 10,500 (NRTI) or 27,000 (PI) mutants).
abstract_sentence: The study used a large clinical dataset with approximately 300,000 drug-mutant bioactivity data points covering multiple drug classes and thousands of HIV mutants.

fact: Our PCM models achieved prediction errors below 0.5 Log Fold Change and performed better than sequence-only models in resistance classification.
source_span: Our models achieved a prediction error below 0.5 Log Fold Change. Moreover, when directly compared with previously published sequence data derived models PCM performed better in resistance classification and prediction of Log Fold Change (0.76 log units versus 0.91).
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric models achieved a prediction error below 0.5 Log Fold Change and outperformed sequence-only models in resistance classification and prediction accuracy.

fact: The models confirmed known and discovered new resistance mutations in HIV Reverse Transcriptase and Protease.
source_span: Furthermore, we were able to successfully confirm both known and identify previously unpublished, resistance-conferring mutations of HIV Reverse Transcriptase (e.g. K102Y, T216M) and HIV Protease (e.g. Q18N, N88G) from our dataset.
abstract_sentence: The models confirmed known and identified previously unpublished resistance-conferring mutations in HIV Reverse Transcriptase and HIV Protease.

fact: The models predicted drug resistance correctly in 84% of cases on the Stanford HIV resistance database, better than previous methods.
source_span: Finally, we applied our models prospectively to the public HIV resistance database from Stanford University obtaining a correct resistance prediction rate of 84% on the full set (compared to 80% in previous work on a high quality subset). Our model classifies the response correctly in 84% of the cases ( Table 5 ) . The average performance when grouped per individual drug class was very good ( PI 85% , NNRTI 89% and NRTI 79% ) .
abstract_sentence: Applying the models prospectively to the public Stanford HIV resistance database resulted in an 84% correct resistance prediction rate, outperforming previous work.

fact: Proteochemometric models accurately predict phenotypic resistance from genotypic data, including for novel mutants and mixtures.
source_span: We conclude that proteochemometric models are able to accurately predict the phenotypic resistance based on genotypic data even for novel mutants and mixtures.
abstract_sentence: Proteochemometric models can accurately predict phenotypic resistance from genotypic data even for novel HIV mutants and mixtures.

fact: Applicability Domain was extended to biological similarity to inform users about the reliability of PCM model predictions.
source_span: Crucial for the application of computational models is an estimate in which cases the model can be trusted , and where it is likely to fail . In this spirit , the ‘Applicability Domain’ of computational models has become an important topic recently; however , so far it was mainly applied to the chemical domain . This concept was extended in the current work , given the nature of PCM models , also to the protein target or biological domain where special considerations need to be taken into account . At a similarity threshold of 97% each sequence is hence assigned a density score between 0 and 1 ... if the fraction of sequences having this similarity of 97% ( X-axis ) is larger ( closer to 1 ) , the maximal encountered prediction error ( RMSE , y-axis ) is lower ( closer to 0 log units ) . This means that if the model can extrapolate from a larger number of sequences having a similarity of 97% or higher , the predictions become more reliable .
abstract_sentence: The concept of 'Applicability Domain' was extended to include biological similarity measures, allowing assessment of when PCM model predictions for HIV mutants are reliable.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus expresses cell wall-anchored proteins that mediate adhesion, invasion, and immune evasion, contributing to its virulence.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus expresses a number of cell wall-anchored proteins that mediate adhesion and invasion of host cells and tissues and promote immune evasion , consequently contributing to the virulence of this organism .
abstract_sentence: Staphylococcus aureus expresses cell wall-anchored proteins that contribute to its virulence by mediating adhesion, invasion, and immune evasion.

fact: Clumping factor B (ClfB) facilitates Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares.
source_span: The cell wall-anchored protein clumping factor B ( ClfB ) has previously been shown to facilitate S . aureus nasal colonization through high affinity interactions with the cornified envelope in the anterior nares . During nasal colonization , S . aureus binding to the squamous epithelium of the anterior nares is facilitated via the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin [13]. Previous to this study , the main function attributed to ClfB was in facilitating S . aureus nasal colonization due to its ability to bind host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10 in the anterior nares [13–15].
abstract_sentence: Clumping factor B (ClfB) facilitates Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization by binding with high affinity to the cornified envelope protein loricrin in the anterior nares.

fact: The role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI) had not been previously investigated.
source_span: However , the role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection ( SSTI ) has never been investigated .
abstract_sentence: The role of ClfB during skin and soft tissue infection (SSTI) had not been previously investigated.

fact: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs.
source_span: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during SSTIs . This study identifies , for the first time , an important role for ClfB in the pathogenesis of SSTIs and provides proof-of-concept that ClfB represents a good candidate antigen for inclusion in next-generation vaccines targeting S . aureus SSTI. Using a clfB mutant in the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300 strain , LAC::lux , we demonstrate that ClfB is a virulence determinant during S . aureus skin infection.
abstract_sentence: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB as a virulence factor during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.

fact: ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue.
source_span: ClfB is crucial in determining the abscess structure and bacterial burden early in infection and this is dependent upon a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin which is expressed within the abscess tissue . At 48 h post-infection ( Fig 3 ) loricrin is clearly visible in the epidermal layer of the skin ( Fig 3B ) , which is to be expected as it is a major component of the cornified envelope . Interestingly , it is also detected in the abscess wall structure following challenge with both LAC::lux ( Fig 3C ) and LAC::lux ΔclfB ( S2 Fig ). Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that loricrin , an important ligand for ClfB , was present in the outermost layer of the skin , the corneal layer , as expected; however , loricrin also appeared to be present within the wall of the skin abscess structure of LAC::lux infected mice . Although loricrin is normally confined to the granular and corneal layers of the skin [22 , 23] , the expression and localisation of loricrin is disrupted during wound healing [24 , 25]. Taken together , the results of this study highlight the importance of ClfB as a virulence determinant during S . aureus SSTIs which plays a role in determining the bacterial burden at the site of infection but most importantly identifies for the first time how ClfB also affects the structure and formation of the skin abscess . ClfB exerts its effect in the early stage of infection and its interaction with loricrin appears to play a role during pathogenesis
abstract_sentence: ClfB determines abscess structure and bacterial burden early in skin infection through a specific interaction with the ligand loricrin expressed in abscess tissue.

fact: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection .
source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection . Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ ( Fig 6A ) , IL-17 ( Fig 6B ) and IL-22 ( Fig 6C ) producing CD4+ T cells by inguinal lymph node ( ILN ) cells ( skin-draining lymph nodes ) compared to CpG-immunized mice . ClfB-specific CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ , IL-17 and IL-22 were also increased in the ILN of ClfB-vaccinated groups compared to the adjuvant alone group ( S5 Fig ) . Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group ( Fig 7A ). Vaccination with ClfB+CpG also activated humoral immune responses by inducing significant levels of ClfB-specific neutralizing antibodies compared to controls. Mice vaccinated with ClfB in combination with CpG developed significantly smaller abscess lesions throughout the 6-day infection period compared to those vaccinated with adjuvant alone ... and the bacterial burden in the skin of ClfB vaccinated mice was decreased throughout the course of infection as measured by bioluminescence.
abstract_sentence: Vaccination targeting ClfB induces protective humoral and cellular immune responses and leads to protection during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection.

fact: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.
source_span: Dengue virus ( DENV ) is the most prevalent arbovirus leading to an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections every year .
abstract_sentence: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most prevalent arbovirus causing an estimated 100 million symptomatic dengue infections annually.

fact: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).
source_span: DENV can cause a spectrum of clinical manifestations , ranging from mild dengue fever ( DF ) to more life threatening forms such as dengue hemorrhagic fever ( DHF ) .
abstract_sentence: DENV infection can cause a range of clinical manifestations from mild dengue fever (DF) to life-threatening dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF).

fact: The mechanisms triggering the transition from mild dengue fever (DF) to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at the critical phase of infection are not well understood.
source_span: The clinical symptoms of DHF become evident typically at the critical phase of infection ( 5–7 days after onset of fever ) , yet the mechanisms that trigger transition from DF to DHF are not well understood .
abstract_sentence: The mechanisms triggering the transition from mild dengue fever (DF) to severe dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at the critical phase of infection are not well understood.

fact: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling was performed on sera from adult DF and DHF patients at critical and recovery phases.
source_span: We performed a mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of infection . In the present study , metabolomics investigation was conducted on the same patient cohort at the critical phase ( day 5–7 post onset of fever ) and recovery phase ( day 21–28 post onset of fever ) to map the serum metabolome and identify metabolic pathways linked to dengue progression .
abstract_sentence: The study performed mass spectrometry-based metabolomic profiling of sera from adult DF and DHF patients at the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection.

fact: Twenty-nine metabolites differed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase, including bile acids and other metabolite classes.
source_span: There were 29 differentially expressed metabolites identified between DF and DHF at the critical phase . These include bile acids , purines , acylcarnitines , phospholipids , and amino acids . In the critical phase, a total of 29 MSI Levels 1 and 2 metabolites, were significantly expressed between DHF and DF patients, were identified.
abstract_sentence: Twenty-nine metabolites were differentially expressed between DF and DHF patients at the critical phase, including bile acids, purines, acylcarnitines, phospholipids, and amino acids.

fact: Bile acids were up to 5 fold higher in DHF patients and correlated with higher AST and ALT levels, suggesting liver injury.
source_span: Bile acids were observed up to 5 fold higher levels among DHF compared to DF patients and were significantly correlated to the higher levels of aspartate transaminase ( AST ) and alanine transaminase ( ALT ) , suggestive of liver injury among DHF . Furthermore, these bile acids demonstrated positive correlations to AST and ALT levels, indicating they may be associated with liver dysfunction in DHF. Put together , elevated bile acids among DHF patients and their positive correlations to AST and ALT levels indicated that these bile acids may play an important role in liver pathology in DHF patients . In the clinic , liver enlargement and elevated transaminases have been used as the clinical features of hepatic histological changes in dengue patients [31] , and we indeed found in this study that AST and ALT levels were significantly higher in DHF than in DF .
abstract_sentence: Bile acids were up to fivefold higher in DHF patients compared to DF patients at the critical phase and correlated with elevated liver enzymes AST and ALT, indicating liver injury in DHF.

fact: Uric acid was 1.5 fold lower in DHF patients than DF patients, indicating decreased antioxidant defense.
source_span: Uric acid , the most abundant antioxidant in the blood , was observed to be 1 . 5 fold lower among DHF compared to DF patients . This could result in decreased capacity of endogenous antioxidant defense and elevated oxidative stress among DHF patients .
abstract_sentence: Uric acid, the most abundant antioxidant in blood, was 1.5 fold lower in DHF patients compared to DF patients, suggesting reduced antioxidant defense and increased oxidative stress in DHF.

fact: DHF patients show increased ROS and NOS, indicating higher oxidative stress.
source_span: Indeed , increased ROS and NOS have been reported in DHF patients [37] .
abstract_sentence: Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and nitric oxide species (NOS) have been reported in DHF patients, indicating elevated oxidative stress.

fact: Eight metabolites including bile acid chenodeoxyglycocholic acid remained altered in DHF patients during recovery, suggesting lasting liver effects.
source_span: In the recovery phase , the levels of eight metabolites were still significantly higher or lower among DHF patients , including chenodeoxyglycocholic acid , one of the bile acids observed at the critical phase . This indicates potential prolonged adverse impact on the liver due to DENV infection in DHF patients .
abstract_sentence: At the recovery phase, levels of eight metabolites, including the bile acid chenodeoxyglycocholic acid, remained significantly altered in DHF patients, indicating prolonged liver impact.

fact: Altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF were identified in critical and recovery phases, revealing host-virus interaction differences.
source_span: Our study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF in the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection and provided insights into the different host and DENV interactions between DF and DHF .
abstract_sentence: The study identified altered metabolic pathways linked to DHF during both critical and recovery phases, providing insights into host-virus interactions and DHF pathogenesis.

fact: Altered metabolic pathways may serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF.
source_span: These results provide insights into the mechanisms of DHF pathogenesis , and certain altered pathways might serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF .
abstract_sentence: The identified altered metabolic pathways provide insights into DHF pathogenesis and may serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF.

fact: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs and prevent sequestration of core components.
source_span: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases ( CRLs ) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs . Unbalanced levels can lead to sequestration of CRL core components by a few overabundant substrate receptors .
abstract_sentence: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs.

fact: Misregulation of substrate receptor components of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, has been associated with numerous diseases including cancer.
source_span: Numerous diseases , including cancer , have been associated with misregulation of substrate receptor components , particularly for the largest class of CRLs , the SCF ligases .
abstract_sentence: Misregulation of substrate receptor components of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, has been associated with numerous diseases including cancer.

fact: F-box proteins, the substrate receptors of SCF ligases, are regulated by autocatalytic ubiquitylation within intact SCF complexes followed by proteasome-mediated degradation.
source_span: One relevant mechanism that controls abundance of their substrate receptors , the F-box proteins , is autocatalytic ubiquitylation by intact SCF complex followed by proteasome-mediated degradation .
abstract_sentence: F-box proteins, the substrate receptors of SCF ligases, are regulated by autocatalytic ubiquitylation within intact SCF complexes followed by proteasome-mediated degradation.

fact: Disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction, by cadmium stress or mutations, induces rapid degradation of Met30 via a Skp1-independent ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
source_span: Cadmium exposure leads to dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 thereby generating a burst of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30, which needs to be controlled by the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway. We were interested in how cells cope with the generated excess of Met30 because the well-described autocatalytic F-box protein degradation pathway mechanism cannot act on Met30 during these conditions . Interestingly , degradation of the F-box protein Met30 was maintained and even slightly induced in response to cadmium stress . A mutant form of Met30 lacking its entire F-box domain ( Met30ΔFbox ) was constitutively unstable even though cells did not experience cadmium stress . Rapid degradation of Met30ΔFbox was observed both in cycloheximide chase and promoter shut-off experiments , indicating that components of this degradation pathway are constitutively present and that new protein synthesis is not required . Collectively these results demonstrate that disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction , by either active signal-induced dissociation ( cadmium stress ) or by mutations in Met30 or Skp1 , induces rapid degradation of the F-box protein Met30 .
abstract_sentence: A Skp1-independent degradation pathway targets Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1, maintaining its degradation even under cadmium stress.

fact: An additional degradation pathway for Met30 dissociated from Skp1 requires Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of Skp1, with Cdc53 able to bind Met30 directly and mediate its degradation.
source_span: Here we describe an additional pathway for regulation of F-box proteins on the example of yeast Met30 . This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1 . Unexpectedly , this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1 . Together these results suggest existence of a novel mechanism of Met30 regulation that specifically targets Met30 that is displaced from Skp1 and is dependent on the ubiquitin proteasome system and requires the function of Cdc53 , Rbx1 and Cdc34 , but not Skp1 . The experiments with skp1 single and skp1 cdc53 double mutants strongly suggested that the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway for Met30 was dependent on Cdc53 and independent of Skp1 Not only was Met30 degradation active in the absence of Skp1 in vivo, but in addition a Cdc53 mutant incapable of binding to Skp1 could fully complement the Met30 degradation defect of cdc53 mutants. In addition, Cdc53/Rbx1 can directly bind Met30 in the absence of Skp1 in vitro and binding depends on the degron region adjacent to the F-box motif.
abstract_sentence: The Skp1-independent degradation pathway requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but not Skp1, showing a novel function of Cdc53.

fact: This non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress in yeast.
source_span: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress . Cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E were significantly more sensitive and exhibited a growth arrest in response to cadmium stress. In addition to enhanced cadmium sensitivity, Met30M178E/I179E mutants displayed increased chromosome loss.
abstract_sentence: The Skp1-independent, Cul1-dependent degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and defense against heavy metal stress.

fact: The SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1, along with the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34, are involved in the Skp1-independent ubiquitylation and degradation of unbound Met30, suggesting a novel function of Cdc53/Cul1.
source_span: This degradation pathway targets Met30 that is detached from Skp1 and involves the SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1 , as well as the cognate SCF ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 . Importantly , this ubiquitylation pathway does not require Skp1 ( Skp1-independent Cul1-dependent ubiquitylation ) and suggests a function of Cdc53/Cul1 that is independent from association with Skp1 . Met30 can interact with Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro at a site distinct from the Skp1 binding domain of Cdc53. Together, our findings shed light on the regulation and complexity of E3 ligases and suggest additional diversity in the cullin-RING family of ubiquitin ligases.
abstract_sentence: The SCF core components Cdc53, Rbx1, and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 mediate Skp1-independent ubiquitylation and degradation of unbound Met30, revealing additional diversity in cullin-RING ligases.
